seo.title: Compare TablePro with other database clients
seo.description: TablePro compared with TablePlus, DBeaver, DataGrip, Navicat, Beekeeper Studio, Sequel Ace, Postico, HeidiSQL and phpMyAdmin, with dated facts and sources.

header.title: Compare TablePro with other database clients
header.lead: Each comparison says where the other client fits better, where TablePro differs and what TablePro does not do. Facts about other products come from official sources and carry the date they were checked.

bySituation.title: Choose by situation
bySituation.lead: One line for each client. Each links to the full comparison.
bySituation.tablepro: Choose TablePro if you want an open-source client with a native Mac app and a separate iPhone and iPad app. The AI assistant and the MCP server are free in the Mac app, and it imports saved connections from {apps}.

items.tableplus: Choose TablePlus if you also work on Windows or Linux, or connect to Vertica or Greenplum.
items.dbeaver: Choose DBeaver if you want a free client for Windows, macOS and Linux that connects to any engine with a JDBC driver.
items.datagrip: Choose DataGrip if you want a database IDE from JetBrains with version control built in, and your work is non-commercial or you already pay for JetBrains tools.
items.navicat: Choose Navicat if you need data modeling or Navicat Cloud for working with a team, and a perpetual license fits your budget.
items.beekeeper-studio: Choose Beekeeper Studio if you want an open-source client that works the same way on Windows, macOS and Linux.
items.sequel-ace: Choose Sequel Ace if you only use MySQL and MariaDB and want a free, open-source Mac app from the Mac App Store.
items.sequel-pro: Still on Sequel Pro? Its last release, {status.version}, dates from {status.date}. Sequel Ace continues it, and TablePro imports Sequel Ace connections.
items.postico: Choose Postico if you only use PostgreSQL and want a focused Mac app with a one-time license.
items.heidisql: Choose HeidiSQL if you already use it on Windows and want the same free client on a Mac with Apple silicon.
items.phpmyadmin: Choose phpMyAdmin if you manage MySQL or MariaDB in a web browser, for example on hosting that provides it through cPanel.
items.mysql-workbench: Choose MySQL Workbench if you want Oracle’s own tool for MySQL, with SQL notebooks and MySQL Enterprise Backup integration.
items.pgadmin: Choose pgAdmin if PostgreSQL is all you use and you want its debugger, pgAgent jobs or a web server that several people share.
items.dbgate: Choose DbGate if you want an open-source client for Windows, macOS and Linux that also runs as a web app.
items.mongodb-compass: Choose MongoDB Compass if MongoDB is your only database and you build aggregation pipelines stage by stage or study a collection’s schema.
items.ssms: Choose SQL Server Management Studio, on Windows, for SQL Server Agent and Always On. It has no Mac version, and on a Mac Microsoft points to Visual Studio Code with the MSSQL extension.

openSource.title: Open-source clients on Mac
openSource.lead: These clients publish their source code under an open-source license. Sequel Pro is no longer maintained, and phpMyAdmin runs on a web server that you open in a browser.

switching.title: Switching to TablePro
switching.body: TablePro imports saved connections from {apps}, including saved passwords. Navicat connections come from a file you export in Navicat.
switching.none: There is no importer for {others}. Add those connections by hand, or paste a connection URL.

method.title: How these pages are written
paragraphs: Every fact about another product comes from an official source: the product’s own website, documentation, repository, release notes or store listing, or the package manager or platform vendor that distributes it. Each page lists its sources with the date they were checked.
TablePro’s side comes from the same data as the rest of this site, so its prices, platforms and features match the pricing and feature pages.
There are no speed, memory or startup figures, because no measurement of these clients that others can reproduce was found to cite.
Prices and features change. If something here is out of date, <issues>open an issue on GitHub</issues>.
